texto:
Advertisers certified under Google's Gambling and games policy will be able to run online gambling campaigns in YouTube's top-of-homepage slot from October 21, 2026, according to a notice Google posted on October 7. Google describes the change as an expansion of an existing allowance for sports betting, and it leaves out one group: advertisers of online-gambling promoting content who are not subject to mandatory state or national gambling registration.
In Short
YouTube is loosening a rule so that online gambling companies approved by Google can buy the large banner at the top of its homepage, starting October 21, 2026. Until now that banner has been open to sports betting but closed to most other kinds of online gambling, so the change matters to gambling brands that want the slot and to anyone who opens YouTube and sees it. Approved advertisers can be booked into the placement from October 21, while the usual age, legal and local rules still apply, and the notice does not say which countries are included.
What the notice says
Google published the notice on its Advertising Policies Help pages on October 7, 2026, under the heading "Updates to YouTube Masthead Ad Requirements (October 2026)". The start date sits 14 days later. The text is short: one sentence announcing the change, one placing it in relation to earlier rules, and one on compliance.
According to the notice, YouTube's ad requirements will be updated on October 21 "to permit Masthead advertisements for online gambling who are certified under our Gambling and games policy". The next sentence reads: "This expands upon the platform's existing allowance for sports betting."
The first of those sentences is missing a word. The phrase "online gambling who are certified" has no noun to attach to. The page's own machine-generated summary, labelled "Summarized by Google AI" and "Beta", supplies one: "Effective October 21, 2026, YouTube Masthead ads will permit certified online gambling advertisers." The reading is the obvious one, yet it comes from the summary rather than the policy text, and a note on the page says the English version is the official language used to enforce Google Ads policies.
The exclusion
A parenthetical removes "advertisers of online-gambling promoting content who are not subject to mandatory state or national gambling registration requirements". The distinction rests on how Google sorts gambling advertisers. According to ReadWrite, the policy revision that Google released on February 10, 2025 and that took effect on April 14, 2025 covers three areas: online gambling, offline gambling and online gambling-promoting content. The new Masthead notice speaks to the first and the third. About offline gambling it says nothing.
Read literally, the exclusion applies to promoters who face no registration duty. Promoters that do face one are not named in it, and whether they qualify is left to the certification condition. That is an inference from the wording, not a statement in the notice.
The last sentence on compliance is blunt: "All online gambling ads must fully comply with the broader Gambling and Games policy and adhere to all legal, jurisdictional, and age restrictions." The notice closes with "This policy change will take effect on October 21, 2026."
A widening in steps
The Masthead began as a closed door for gambling. When PPC Land reported Google's Masthead-specific content requirements in June 2021, the prohibited categories included gambling - offline, online, online non-casino games and social casino - alongside elections and politics, alcohol, and prescription drug terms.
The first exception arrived on September 6, 2022. According to a Google help notice of that date, sports betting became permissible on the Masthead with immediate effect, subject to the Gambling and games policy. Roughly 14 months separated the blanket prohibition from the first carve-out.
Later steps happened partly on a neighbouring surface. In April 2025, Google TV Masthead was opened to sports betting ads in the United States from April 30, a format governed by its own rules. By then the YouTube Masthead already carried sports betting exceptions, along with daily fantasy sports exceptions for Canada, India and the United States, and more than 30 US states plus the District of Columbia had legalised sports betting at that point.
Then came the extension of Google TV Masthead sports betting and daily fantasy sports to the UK and Brazil, announced on October 28, 2025 and effective November 13, 2025. UK operators needed registration with the Gambling Commission and a valid operating licence number, while Brazil required authorisation. Northern Ireland was excluded.
The October 21 change lands just over four years after the first exception. The notice frames it as a continuation of that exception, not as a new category.
Lead times have varied along the way. The 2022 sports betting allowance applied immediately. The April 2025 Google TV Masthead change took effect 16 days after its announcement, the UK and Brazil extension also 16 days after, and the YouTube Masthead change comes 14 days after its posting.
What the notice leaves unstated
Markets
The notice names no countries. Its reference to "mandatory state or national gambling registration requirements" points toward places where operators or promoters register at state level, as in the United States, or at national level. That reading is an inference, not something Google states. Both of the earlier Google TV Masthead announcements named their markets - the United States in April 2025, then the UK and Brazil in October 2025. The Masthead notice does not.
For scale, ReadWrite said the policy lists 55 countries in total, counting the United States, where gambling-related advertising is approved. Whether Masthead eligibility will follow that list, or something narrower, is not addressed.
Certification
The notice refers only to certification under the Gambling and games policy. Yet the page's suggested questions include "How do I apply for YouTube Masthead certification?", and the notice does not say whether that describes a step separate from gambling certification.
On the TV side, certification did not work as a single global approval. The Google TV Masthead rules for the UK and Brazil required one application per country, allowed an account to be certified for online gambling or for social casino games but not both, and required recertification after material changes. Whether the same mechanics will govern the YouTube Masthead is not stated.
Adjacent categories and formats
Daily fantasy sports, social casino games and online non-casino games are not mentioned. Nor is Google TV Masthead. Unless Google revises those rules separately, the two formats would diverge: certified online gambling on the YouTube Masthead, and sports betting, plus daily fantasy sports in the UK and Brazil, on Google TV Masthead.
How the slot is sold and policed
A PPC Land analysis from March 2026 described the Masthead as reservation-only, booked through a Google sales representative and priced on a cost-per-thousand-impressions (CPM) or cost-per-hour (CPH) basis. The format autoplays for up to 30 seconds on desktop without sound and for its full duration on mobile.
Pricing mechanics have moved over the years. In July 2019, Google rolled out Masthead buying on a CPM basis worldwide, where before the placement had been sold by the day. A December 2023 update made cost-per-impression Masthead buying available through Google Ads reservation.
Enforcement runs asset by asset. When Google reorganised its YouTube and Discover ad requirements on September 30, 2025, with no change to enforcement, Masthead assets were reviewed individually, requirements could be stricter than on other surfaces, and an asset disapproved for the Masthead might still run on other Google properties.
Certification in 2026
The October notice arrives in a year when Google has been tightening the gating around gambling certification. According to a Google notice posted on January 22, 2026 and effective March 23, 2026, accounts in any gambling and games category must demonstrate good policy health. Manager accounts (MCCs) with significant volumes of revoked certificates lose the ability to apply, and their existing certifications are revoked.
A further update followed. According to iGamingExpert, which covered the change on September 15, 2026, Google set out in July a rule scheduled for September 14, 2026 that extends the certification requirements across all categories under the Gambling and games policy. iGamingExpert also listed domain rules: free subdomains are ineligible, the domain must be directly owned and controlled by the business, and domains unrelated to gambling are ineligible. Certified accounts, it said, must regularly review ad and keyword statuses.
The Masthead notice itself does not describe how these account-level rules interact with the new permission.
Why it matters to the marketing community
The Masthead is a single reserved placement at the top of the YouTube homepage rather than a line in an auction, so the category rules act as a gate on who can be booked at all. The notice moves that gate for one regulated category. YouTube's wider advertising business gives the placement its context: the platform recorded ad revenue of $10.3 billion in Q3 2025, up 15% year on year.
Several practical unknowns remain for the people who plan and sell this inventory. Which markets are in scope? Does a Masthead-specific certification exist? Do social casino games and daily fantasy sports follow the same rule? And how will age restrictions be applied to a placement shown on a homepage? The notice gives none of those answers, and the 14 days between posting and the start date leave little time for the details to emerge before the rule applies.
There is also a regulatory dimension. The notice ties the permission to "all legal, jurisdictional, and age restrictions", which hands much of the practical boundary to local law. Registration regimes differ across US states and national jurisdictions, and the carve-out for unregistered promoters reflects that.
The page's own suggested prompts include "Why are certain gambling ads restricted on the YouTube Masthead?" The notice offers no reason for the change itself.
Timeline
- July 28, 2019: Google rolls out YouTube Masthead buying on a CPM basis globally, after sales by cost per day
- June 27, 2021: Google publishes Masthead-specific content requirements, listing gambling among prohibited categories
- September 6, 2022: Google allows sports betting on the YouTube Masthead, subject to the Gambling and games policy
- December 19, 2023: cost-per-impression Masthead buying becomes available through Google Ads reservation
- February 10, 2025: Google releases revised gambling advertising guidelines, effective April 14, 2025
- April 14, 2025: Google announces sports betting ads on Google TV Masthead in the United States, effective April 30, 2025
- September 30, 2025: Google reorganises its YouTube and Discover ad requirements, with no change to enforcement
- October 28, 2025: Google announces sports betting and daily fantasy sports ads on Google TV Masthead in the UK and Brazil, effective November 13, 2025
- January 22, 2026: Google posts a notice requiring good policy health for accounts in any gambling and games category, effective March 23, 2026
- July 2026: Google sets out a further certification update scheduled for September 14, 2026
- October 7, 2026: Google posts the notice on YouTube Masthead ad requirements
- October 21, 2026: certified online gambling advertisers become eligible for the Masthead

Summary
- Who: Google and YouTube; advertisers certified under the Gambling and games policy. Advertisers of online-gambling promoting content that is not subject to mandatory state or national gambling registration are excluded.
- What: YouTube's ad requirements will permit Masthead advertisements for certified online gambling, expanding the existing allowance for sports betting. All ads must comply with the Gambling and Games policy and with legal, jurisdictional and age restrictions.
- When: The notice was posted on October 7, 2026, and the change takes effect on October 21, 2026.
- Where: The YouTube Masthead. The notice names no countries and does not mention Google TV Masthead.
- Why: The notice gives no reason. It presents the change as an extension of the existing sports betting allowance.
